title: Credential propagation matrix and iterable safety with SDK ergonomics bump
author: Sophie Chen
release_notes: Introduce credential propagation matrix across Python/TS/Go SDKs to standardize fallback behavior; attach lightweight provenance to streaming iterables to enable safe retry/resume; bump SDK versions: py->1.10.0, ts->2.6.0, go->v0.10.0; opt-out via REDWOOD_CRED_MATRIX=0.
description: Context: This PR implements a cross-SDK credential propagation matrix and a minimal provenance envelope on streaming iterables to make credential selection deterministic and safe during retry/resume flows. Motivation: observed parity gaps where TypeScript and Python returned different credential choices during fast failover which caused double-in-flight tokens and intermittent auth errors in production; fixing parity prevents client-level duplicate reauth attempts and reduces error noise. Scope: Python, TypeScript, Go SDKs plus core retry-presets library, integration tests, docs, and CI. High level changes: 1) API: introduce CredMatrix (SDK-visible) and attach a 3-field provenance header to iterable payloads to carry origin/lease/slot metadata; 2) Core: centralized retry-presets mapping that selects preferred credential mode by workload hint; 3) Perf: micro-optimization to avoid temporary JSON allocations when materializing provenance on hot paths; 4) Tests: cross-language e2e harness for resume+reauth and new unit matrices to validate fallback permutations; 5) Docs: migration guide and changelog entry. Checklist: [x] unit tests added for py/ts/go [x] integration harness [x] docs updated with migration notes [x] changelog entry created [x] API compatibility checked. Commits summary: - feat(cred): introduce CredMatrix core, credential mode enum and selection rules - feat(py): attach provenance envelope to streaming Iterable in Python SDK and expose opt-out env var - feat(ts): mirror cred matrix and add provenance header to stream wrapper with TypeScript-friendly types - feat(go): add matrix consumer and ensure zero-copy header attach path for streams - refactor(core): move retry-presets and mapping into retry-presets package - perf: avoid JSON allocations in provenance serialization - test: add cross-language resume+reauth e2e harness - docs: migration guide and examples Changed files (high level): sdk/python/redwood/credentials/cred_matrix.py sdk/python/redwood/streaming/provenance.py sdk/python/setup.py sdk/typescript/src/credentials/credMatrix.ts sdk/typescript/src/streaming/provenance.ts sdk/typescript/package.json sdk/go/credentials/matrix.go sdk/go/streaming/provenance.go core/retry-presets/matrix.go core/retry-presets/README.md tests/integration/cred_matrix_resume_test.py tests/integration/cred_matrix_resume_test.ts tests/integration/cred_matrix_resume_test.go docs/sdk-migrations/cred-propagation-matrix.md ci/workflows/e2e-sdk-matrix.yml ci/scripts/run-cross-sdk-harness.sh changeset.yaml (release bumps) Review conversation summary: Miguel Ortega: "Can you explain the provenance envelope format and why it's minimal?" Author (Sophie): "Three fields: origin (sdk:py/ts/go), lease_id (optional short token id), slot_seq (small int). Kept compact to avoid token blowup in headers and to remain O(1) to serialize in hot paths." Daniel Kim: "How does this interact with existing session-lease logic?" Author: "CredMatrix sits upstream of session-lease selection; if a session-lease is present it still wins, but matrix provides deterministic fallback ordering when lease is absent or expired." Asha Patel: "Any perf impact on high throughput streaming?" Author: "Benchmarks included: <1% p99 impact after avoiding JSON allocations; go path is zero-copy and TS/py use compact binary header if available." Requested changes: add explicit opt-out env var, document migration steps, tighten type defs in TS. Resolution: opt-out env REDWOOD_CRED_MATRIX=0 added, TS typedefs tightened, migration doc expanded. CI: unit(py) passed, unit(ts) initial run had 2 flaky tests failing, rerun passed, unit(go) passed, lint passed for all, e2e cross-sdk harness passed, perf smoke tests passed. Merge: merged via squash on 2025-01-22 after approvals from Miguel Ortega and Daniel Kim. Version bumps: Python 1.9.0 -> 1.10.0, TypeScript 2.5.1 -> 2.6.0, Go v0.9.8 -> v0.10.0. Migration notes: consumers that depend on internal credential selection may need to opt-in to the new matrix by removing custom credential hooks or setting REDWOOD_CRED_MATRIX=0 during gradual rollout; recommended quick test: run resume e2e harness locally. Related tickets: ENG-4422 (parity fixes), ENG-4470 (retry policy mapping).
